subject: PulseCare due diligence: data segregation, de-id pipeline, and BAA timeline
messages:
From: Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@pulsecare.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@pulsecare.health
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RFI: data segregation, de-id, and BAA questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — we're starting a formal due-diligence pass as part of PulseCare's evaluation for hosting PHI-driven clinical NLP workloads. The procurement/security team pulled together the items below. Can you confirm the following and attach any short artifacts/examples you have (architecture diagrams, sample audit logs, de-identification overview):

1) Customer data segregation: how do you ensure tenant isolation at the networking, storage, and logging layers? Do you support per-customer VPCs and storage partitions?
2) De-identification pipeline: what out-of-the-box tooling or patterns do you provide for name/identifier redaction, date shifting, and pseudonymization? Any published algorithms or config examples?
3) Re-identification controls: can keys for tokenization/deterministic pseudonyms be locked to HSM/KMS and audited?
4) Audit evidence: sample log extract showing access events for PHI, with retention controls and redaction applied where appropriate.
5) BAA and timeline: we need a BAA addendum to our master services agreement — what is your typical turnaround and negotiation cadence?
6) Deployment residency: can Redwood run in our us-east region and do you offer an on-prem/private appliance for stricter isolation?

We attached PulseCare_RFI_v1.pdf with our scoring rubric. Looking for a short written response + materials by EOW (this Friday) if possible. If it helps, we can schedule an architecture call.

Best,
Emma Zhao
Senior Procurement Manager
PulseCare Health

Subject: Re: Initial RFI: data segregation, de-id, and BAA questions

Emma — thanks for the clear list and the RFI. High-level answers below and we've attached a short reference packet (redwood-deid-overview.pdf) and schedule proposal. Marissa and Laura are looped in for technical detail.

Quick answers (summary):
- Tenant isolation: we support dedicated VPCs for Private deployments and strict tenant tagging for Hosted/Dedicated with storage partitioning and per-customer encryption keys.
- De-id: Redwood provides a configurable de-identification pipeline (redaction, date-shifting, tokenization) that runs as a pre-processing step before data is persisted or routed to model instances. We include presets for healthcare (PHI types) and allow custom regex / rulesets.
- Re-identification/KMS: deterministic pseudonymization keys can be stored in customer-managed KMS/HSMs (Private) or our managed KMS with HSM backing (Hosted). All key usage is audited.
- Audit logs: we can provide sample access logs and a map of where audit evidence is stored; retention policies are configurable per-customer.
- BAA timeline: typical turnaround is 2–3 weeks for our standard BAA addendum with parallel legal review; custom redlines may extend the timeline and we handle SLA/insurance items in the same window.
- Residency: yes — us-east region is supported for Hosted; Private (VPC or on-prem) is available for stricter isolation.

Next steps I'd suggest:
1) Marissa to provide detailed de-id and logging examples.
2) Laura to propose an architecture call and demo slot (30–45m).
3) I'll send our standard BAA draft and a HubSpot link for tracking.

Can you confirm expected daily throughput (approx requests per minute) and sample PHI types you'll be sending (e.g., free text clinical notes, structured identifiers)? That will help us scope the architecture notes.

Thanks — would love to get the materials to you by EOW.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: data segregation, de-id, and BAA questions

Kimberly / team — detailed technical notes below for PulseCare. I've attached a short sample audit log and an architecture diagram that illustrates physical separation options for Private.

1) Tenant isolation (networking/storage/logging)- Networking: Private deployments run in customer-managed VPCs with dedicated subnets and security groups. For Dedicated/Hosted we provide VPC peering or private connectivity and strict network policies limiting egress to customer endpoints.
- Storage: object stores are partitioned by tenant; for Private we recommend separate buckets/volumes per customer. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256; encryption keys are per-tenant and rotated per policy.
- Logging: audit streams are tagged with tenant-id; access logs for PHI events are written to a dedicated, append-only audit store. Logs can be exported to the customer's SIEM.

2) De-identification pipeline- Overview: inbound data passes through a pre-ingest pipeline consisting of (a) syntactic redaction (regex-based PHI detection), (b) probabilistic NER-based PHI detection for edge cases, (c) deterministic tokenization/pseudonymization for identifiers, and (d) optional reversible token vaulting when re-identification is required under controlled workflows.
- Config: customers can select presets (clinical-notes, claims, imaging-metadata) and add custom rules. The pipeline runs before any unencrypted persistence.
- Algorithms & examples: we use open-source NER models tuned for PHI, combined with rule-based enrichments. Deterministic tokens are produced using HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the tenant key (truncated), stored only as token hashes; re-identification requires an HSM-backed unwrap.

3) Key management & re-id controls- Keys can be in customer-managed KMS (recommended for Private) or our managed KMS (Hosted). For sensitive customers we support customer HSM-backed master keys; key usage generates audit events. Re-identification is gated by RBAC, approval workflows, and is logged with requestor identity + Justification tag.

4) Audit evidence & retention- Sample log (attached): shows read/write events with tenant id, actor, operation, resource, and redaction flag. Retention policies are configurable (30/90/365 days) and we support export to S3/Blob for long-term archival. We also provide periodic attestation exports for SOC2/HIPAA audits.

5) On-prem and isolation options- We offer an on-prem appliance package (compressed container bundle with orchestration templates) for air-gapped deployments. Private VPC deployments give the same controls but with remote managed control-plane options.

Known limitations & trade-offs:
- Live re-identification (reversible tokens) has higher audit and process overhead — recommend reversible token use only when necessary.
- NER-based redaction reduces recall risks but needs domain tuning; sample false-positive/false-negative rates are documented in the attached note.

Attachments: sample_audit_log.txt; architecture_vpc_partitioning.png; deid_ruleset_example.yaml

Let me know if PulseCare wants a short technical walkthrough of the pipeline — we can demo the de-identification UI and show sample before/after examples.

—Marissa
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial RFI: data segregation, de-id, and BAA questions

Emma — great questions. Quick responses and concrete next steps below: 

- Deterministic tokenization & date-shifting: tokens are deterministic per-tenant+salt (so the same identifier maps consistently within a tenant) using HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant keys. Date-shifting is configurable: default mode is consistent offset per patient record (to preserve relative intervals) but we also support randomized windowing for extra privacy. We'll send a short appendix with pseudo-code and example outputs in the technical packet.
- Re-identification approval: re-id requests require an RBAC-checked API call plus an approval workflow. By default we support 1 approver, and we can enable multi-approver gating for high-sensitivity roles (configurable for Private deployments). All operations are logged with justification text and operator identity.
- EU residency: we have EU-hosted capacity in the Dublin region; provisioning typically takes 1–2 weeks once commercial terms and a BAA are signed. On-prem remains available for customers needing air-gapped controls.

Next steps/ask from PulseCare:
1) Confirm preferred residency (us-east vs eu-dublin) and expected peak RPS so we can size demo.
2) Accept a 45-minute technical walkthrough next Tuesday or Wednesday (Marissa and Laura will lead). Proposed slots: Tue 2027-05-25 10:00–10:45 PDT or Wed 2027-05-26 14:00–14:45 PDT.
3) I'll share our standard BAA draft via DocuSign and the HubSpot deal for signatures. Please expect an initial BAA draft in your inbox shortly.

I've uploaded a starting BAA draft to DocuSign here: https://docusign.net/ABC-123-pulsecare-baa and a working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_drive_link. HubSpot record: https://hubspot.redwood.com/contacts/HS-78421.

Rishi will follow up on commercial cadence and Laura will coordinate the demo. Looking forward to next steps.
